summary: Inverts the exported canDelete(role) authorization predicate in permissions.ts, flipping it from admin-only to all non-admin roles. — Inverts the exported canDelete(role) authorization predicate in permissions.ts, flipping it from admin-only to all non-admin roles.

findings.title: Inverted canDelete grants delete to non-admins, denies admins
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported predicate was `role === "admin"` (delete permitted only for admins) and now returns `role !== "admin"`. Substituting real values: canDelete("admin") === false (admin wrongly denied the destructive action) and canDelete("user") === true (any non-admin/guest role wrongly granted delete). Any consumer that gates a destructive delete on this authorization function now permits deletion for unauthorized roles (privilege escalation / unauthorized destructive action) while blocking the one role that should be allowed. This is the exported public contract, so the inverted promise ships to every importer even though this repo has no in-tree caller.
findings.validation: Assert the contract, e.g. `npx tsx -e "import {canDelete} from './permissions.ts'; if(!(canDelete('admin')===true && canDelete('user')===false)) throw new Error('inverted'); "` or restore `role === "admin"` and re-diff.

checked: EVIDENCE finding: git diff 23f42b1..HEAD -- permissions.ts shows the single changed hunk: line 2 changes `return role === "admin";` to `return role !== "admin";` in exported `canDelete(role: string): boolean` (permissions.ts:1-2). Substituting inputs at HEAD: canDelete("admin") returns false and canDelete("user") returns true, inverting the admin-only authorization for a destructive action. The function is `export`ed, so the inverted boolean is a public contract; rg -n 'canDelete' . returns only the definition, so the security effect on any external delete guard is direct from the changed line.
